character: Historic, high-speed American road course with dramatic elevation changes and the famous Esses sequence. Rewards commitment and smooth inputs through fast, flowing corners.
sources: https://www.imsa.com/watkins-glen/ track facts; The Esses/The Boot/Bus Stop/Inner Loop naming well documented

corners.name: Turn 1
corners.technique: Brake hard from the front straight, late apex to set up the Esses
corners.trap: Over-braking and losing the momentum needed for the following section

corners.name: The Esses
corners.technique: Rhythm and smooth inputs through the direction changes, carry maximum speed
corners.trap: Over-driving any single apex disrupts the whole sequence

corners.name: Bus Stop Chicane
corners.type: tight chicane after the back straight (the Inner Loop)
corners.technique: Hard, late braking, precise through the direction change
corners.trap: Carrying too much speed in and running out of track on exit
corners.note: Lap order: the Inner Loop chicane (T5) comes before The Boot (T8).

corners.name: The Boot
corners.technique: Patient, progressive line as the corner tightens
corners.trap: Early apex leaves nowhere to go as the corner keeps tightening

corners.name: Final Corner
corners.type: final tight corner onto the pit straight
corners.technique: Late apex, clean exit is critical — feeds the start/finish straight
corners.trap: Poor exit here costs time down the entire straight
corners.note: Was named "Inner Loop" — but the Inner Loop is the bus stop chicane at T5 (above); this entry describes the final corner, which is T11.
